After losing Olivia Moultrie to injury, Portland found an explosive dynamic duo capable of pulling off a quarterfinal upset against Washington's vulnerable defense

        Sophia Wilson is back with a vengeance. After missing the 2025 season, she's finished the regular season with the third-most goals in the league, behind only Ashley Sanchez and Barbara Banda. Those 15 goals are an impressive number as she and the Thorns enter the NWSL playoffs, where they'll travel to face the Washington Spirit. But while Wilson and Trinity Rodman will be the headliners of the match, how Portland's attack ticks over is what'll be critical as they try to stop the Spirit from making a run to their third consecutive appearance in the NWSL final in Sunday's quarterfinal matchup.Losing Olivia Moultrie to injury only 16 games into the season was a blow to the squad, but another creative force has stepped forward to lead the attack in 22-year-old midfielder Pietra Tordin. With nine assists and eight goals, she has finished the season with the third-most assists in the league, and her play will be one of the major factors in whether Portland can get past the Spirit. Talent-wise, Washington are expected to win the match, but they can be susceptible to defensive breakdowns, which is when Tordin can strike.  She's already been rewarded with a United States women's national team call-up and made her debut against Spain, and her partnership with Wilson has been the driving force behind Portland's season. Tordin has 51 key passes this season, and 20 of those have been directly to Wilson. Having a striker of Wilson's caliber to pick out does make things easier for Tordin when Portland attack, but Tordin's talent and ability to string plays together make the Thorns quite a dangerous team.
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Playing at home, Adrian Gonzalez and the Spirit will be under pressure, as expectations are high this season. This is a team that is expected to win an NWSL title, and if it doesn't happen, they could be looking for a new coach next season. Gonzalez has done a good job with the squad, but they're built to win. That pressure also makes it tougher to deal with Portland coming to town with the pressure off. The Thorns may be one of the NWSL's most successful teams in history, but in needing to rebound from Moultrie's injury, they're playing with house money. It's exactly the kind of team that can win an NWSL championship if things break their way, and with Tordin in the form that she's in, the Thorns have the talent to go on a run. It all begins with Washington.

title: LaNorris Sellers injury: South Carolina QB returns after exiting vs. Texas A&M - CBS Sports
description: The Gamecocks' star quarterback returned in the second half after leaving Saturday's game in the second quarter
body:
The Gamecocks' star quarterback returned in the second half after leaving Saturday's game in the second quarter
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:57 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The sellout crowd inside Williams-Brice Stadium held its collective breath Saturday in the second quarter after South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers was sandwiched between defenders on a sack against Texas A&M and had to leave the game with an injury.Sellers was slow to get up after losing a fumble on the play at the Aggies' 18-yard line, grabbing his left ankle before hobbling off to the sideline with the help of team trainers. Sellers re-entered the contest to open the third quarter during South Carolina's first possession and showed no ill effects of the first-half injury. Sellers exited the injury tent on his own power, slowly walking toward the locker room with just over four minutes to play before intermission."We're concerned," South Carolina coach Shane Beamer told the ESPN broadcast at halftime. "He's got an ankle, and he's getting an X-ray on it. I don't have anything else."
The Gamecocks (5-3), slotted No. 21 in the first College Football Playoff rankings on the heels of three straight wins, need their best player available the rest of the way to remain in the postseason conversation.Sellers was 10-of-15 for 151 yards and a touchdown in Saturday's game before leaving. Sellers has accounted for 13 touchdowns during South Carolina's current win streak and was named the AP's National Player of the Week last time out after registering 397 yards of total offense and five touchdowns at Oklahoma.
Sellers threw an 84-yard touchdown pass to DJ Black and a 79-yard toss to Mazeo Bennett to highlight his performance. Both plays were made off schedule with Sellers outside of the pocket."Those are great plays. I mean, you worry about those plays from a protection standpoint, so you see him get the ball off," Beamer said after that win. "And I'm proud of our guys, too. When the quarterback scrambles, it's not like everybody just runs around blindly. Like, we have a plan of what needs to happen when the quarterback scrambles, and we worked a lot of that on the bye week. "We talked about it this morning in our staff meeting: that, make sure we're big on scrambles because they're really, really good on defense, and they're probably going to get some pressure on our quarterback, and we've got a chance to hit some big plays in the passing game if we do. So, great to see those guys execute the scramble drills the right way.
This story will be updated as more information becomes available.

title: Kansas City Current advance to NWSL semifinals, end 10 game unbeated streak for Angel City - CBS Sports
description: Kansas City Current advance to NWSL semifinals after extra time penalty in 1-0 win over Angel City FC
body:
Kansas City Current advance to NWSL semifinals after extra time penalty in 1-0 win over Angel City FC
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:17 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Two teams that tied for the most goals scored in the 2026 NWSL regular season played to a narrow scoreline over 120 minutes at CPKC Stadium on Saturday. Kansas City Current, last year's NWSL Shield winners, finally got a playoff win, taking the match 1-0 after extra time. Angel City, with a 10-game unbeaten streak now snapped, say farewell to the postseason.It was a result that maybe doesn't tell the entire story of the potential attacks on the pitch. Both teams scored 54 goals in the regular season, but the quarterfinal quickly turned into a defensive battle destined for a penalty shootout. Instead, the tense game tightened, went to extra time, and a penalty call changed the trajectory when Michelle Cooper converted the kick for the Current.Now the Current avenge last year's home quarterfinal loss, extend their home unbeaten streak to 33 matches, and move on to the semifinal round.Here's how the match unfolded:A defensive game in regulationMany were hoping for fireworks in front of goal, but outside of a few looks, both sides got into dangerous spaces and produced only goalkeeping highlights. One of Kansas City's best chances of the opening half came inside of 20 minutes, as the trio of Haley Hopkins, Temwa Chawinga and Cooper combined for a header that went straight into the hands of goalkeeper Angelina Anderson.
Angel City showed off their impressive defensive shape, limiting the Current's press and slowing the tempo. Both teams at times even stayed more compact than usual, and Current goalkeeper Lorena was also forced to make a key save at the other end, shortly after Chawinga's attempt. 
"It was definitely a team effort. They played a lot of long balls, so winning the second ball was key for us," said Current center back Gabrielle Robinson of the defensive shape."I think our sixes, our front line, was coming back and winning those second balls. But for us, is winning the first one, winning the second, and then turning around and going from there [were keys]. And I thought we were really good with that today."
Angel City's missed opportunityAngel City's midseason turnaround was a main storyline heading into the quarterfinals. The club appointed Leif Gunnar Smerud as interim head coach after parting ways with former manager Alexander Straus, and brought in Ally Sentnor in a summer trade with Kansas City Current.The return of defender Savy King from injury reset the backline, as she slotted in at right back, and pushed Gisele Thompson to play as a wide midfielder for the remainder of the season. Team captain Sarah Gorden elevated her play alongside center back partner Emily Sams, and left back Evelyn Shores led the team with eight assists. Their 10-game unbeaten streak placed them as a team to watch in the playoffs, especially considering the opponent.Angel City beat Kansas City Current earlier in the regular season, then drew 1-1 at CPKC Stadium in August. The group's ability to keep the Current off the scoreboard in regulation was valiant, with Anderson making a massive save in stoppage time of regulation. 
"Listen, I don't always take the opportunity to make an opening statement here, but I did this time because I want to congratulate Angel City on a great season. And it's a shame that one of us on the day was not going to move on. But they're a tough team. They were hard to play against for sure. They gave us everything, and I think we gave them everything," Current manager Chris Armas said in postgame comments."It was a good game, and you can see what it meant to that team. They left everything on the field. So to Leif, the head coach over there, I think he did a great job this season taking over, and they have a lot to be proud of. They're a great team, and just wanted to acknowledge that."Kansas City's playoff momentExtra time proved to be Kansas City's time, even with what some will deem a peculiar penalty call. Plenty of set pieces were awarded during the quarterfinal -- eight corners for Kansas City and 11 for Angel City -- with Angel City midfielder Ary Borges and Current center back Kayla Sharples often jockeying for position in the box.
On a set piece delivery from Izzy Rodriguez, the center official called a penalty for a pushing foul by Angel City keeper Anderson, and after a quick confirmation, the rare call stood and Cooper converted for the Current. 
Cooper's big moment was almost like a passing of the torch, as team captain Lo'eau LaBonta is typically the lead penalty taker. Armas later confirmed in postgame that had the game gone into penalties, the captain would've taken one, but in extra time the moment was Cooper's."[LaBonta] has scored so many in her career. Understands what it feels like at the spot. And even in those moments when she grabs the ball, you know she's maybe protecting Coop in that moment to then hand it off to her. I don't even know if they've had a discussion, but if they did and it went back to Lo, I would trust that she could take it. But this was something ahead of time. We knew Coop would take it, and she buried it," Armas said.
Cooper's big playoff moment was long overdue. The former NWSL Shield winner missed last year's disappointing quarterfinal exit through injury. Now, she's back and with the game-winning goal under her belt."I always want to contribute and help my teammates when I can. So, it was, like, really shitty last year when I got injured, literally right before. But it's part of the game, and I think I supported them the best I could last year. To be able to actually impact the game in a way of scoring a goal in the PK, and converting, it's felt really good. But I think, I can't celebrate yet. We still have two more games to go, one game guaranteed next weekend, and that's honestly the biggest focus for me," Cooper said."I think we can come up with a lot of like reasons and excuses. I could say for last year and why it didn't really fall our way, but I think this team this year has taken things personal and never say die, and that's kind of the mentality that we've been going with, and we just want to keep it rolling. So that's been the biggest change for us, I think, this year," she said.
What's nextKansas City Current will face the winner of Gotham FC vs. Seattle Reign in the semifinal round. The NWSL semifinals will take place on Nov. 14 and 15.

title: NFL fines Jaquan Brisker, two others for illegal Week 8 hits that placed opponents in concussion protocol - CBS Sports
description: Each of the players on the receiving end of those collisions will miss Week 9
body:
Each of the players on the receiving end of those collisions will miss Week 9
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:01 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL levied 31 fines in Week 8, which was the second most in a single week this season. Among the most notable punishments were those handed down to Pittsburgh Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker, Dallas Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown and Las Vegas Raiders safety Jeremy Chinn. Each fine was the result of a hit that led to the offensive player being placed in concussion protocol and ruled out for Week 9.Brisker owes the NFL $17,911 for a blow to the head/neck on Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson. The play occurred less than a minute and a half into the Steelers' victory and drew a roughing the passer penalty, which Brisker voiced extreme displeasure with after the game."Babying the quarterback," Brisker said. "He's laying there crying, whatever he was doing. It is what it is. I assume I'm going to get fined because if you watch it, I'm hitting him with my chest and them I'm off to the side. But he had his binky today, so they threw it out there. It is what it is."Watson briefly left the game, and Shedeur Sanders replaced him. The latter threw two passes before Watson returned to action and finished the game. Although Watson practiced in the days leading up to this Sunday's matchup against the New Orleans Saints and cleared the concussion protocol on Saturday, the Browns announced they will turn to Sanders as their Week 9 starter.
Overshown's fine is for his use of his helmet on a hit against Arizona Cardinals running back Bam Knight. He must pay $9,528. The hit jarred the ball loose from Knight's hands, and the Cowboys recovered the fumble without a penalty. The NFL reviewed the play in the wake of the game, however, and issued the fine.
Knight will not play in the Cardinals' divisional clash with the Seattle Seahawks. He did not practice this week.
Chinn sealed a Raiders win last week with an interception in the end zone, but just one play prior, he made forcible contact with New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson on a catch along the sideline, which resulted in a fine. Chinn owes $17,911 for a hit on a defenseless player. The two players' helmets collided on the play, and while Wilson stayed in the game for the Jets' final snap, he later entered concussion protocol.Wilson reported concussion symptoms the next day, and by midweek the Jets placed him in the protocol. They eventually ruled him out for this week's battle with the Kansas City Chiefs.
There have been 223 plays this season which resulted in a fine. That is 0.0113% of all plays through eight weeks. The 31 fines from Week 8 were second only to the 38 in Week 2.

title: Pick your poison: Rams' Myles Garrett anticipates matchup nightmares in first game with Aaron Donald - CBS Sports
description: An injured reserve stint delayed the first look at Garrett and Donald in the same lineup, but now they could domi
body:
An injured reserve stint delayed the first look at Garrett and Donald in the same lineup, but now they could dominate opposing offenses
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:38 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When Los Angeles Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett returns from injured reserve this week for his first game action since the season opener, he will line up next to defensive lineman Aaron Donald for the first time. That duo is projected to be one of the NFL's most unstoppable tandems at any position since Donald announced that he would come out of retirement for the 2026 season, and now the league will find out just how formidable it really is.The timing of Garrett's IR stint and Donald's season debut clashed, forcing them to wait until November to suit up together. Garrett played just one game before he underwent knee surgery, and Donald entered the lineup in Week 2.Garrett said it will be surreal to share the field with a fellow Defensive Player of the Year award winner."Going into this season, I never thought I'd have the chance," Garrett said ahead of Sunday's road game against the Washington Commanders. "As y'all know, he kept us in suspense for quite a while. It was very exciting to hear about that. Looking forward to the opportunity to get on the field and actually play some real snaps with him."
Garrett's arrival in Los Angeles by way of a blockbuster trade in June was a catalyst for Donald's unretirement, so it is only right that two of the most disruptive players in football history finally get the opportunity to play alongside each other. Donald has been more effective in run defense than pass rushing this season, so with Garrett (the single-season sack record holder) rejoining the fold, their skill sets should complement each other tremendously.Both superstar defenders have commanded double teams at extreme rates throughout their careers, but opposing offensive lines might have to stay more honest with their assignments so as to prevent the other player from capitalizing on the diverted attention."I think offenses really have to pick their poison," Garrett said. "Who's going to be freed up this play? Either of us are pretty good at winning one-on-ones. We'll have some fun."
There is no better time than the present for Garrett to return to full strength and for this duo to join forces. The Rams are in the midst of a potential midseason turnaround after opening the year with a surprising yet immensely disappointing 2-4 record, and they need to keep the momentum rolling to fulfill their Super Bowl expectations.How will Myles Garrett fare in his return?At the time, it was a surprise to see Garrett held entirely in check in the season-opening blowout loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. When the news of his knee ailment came to light, though, it explained why he was held without a single tackle in the contest. Garrett said that the knee acted up on him throughout the game and limited him from making his typical impact as a first-team All-Pro-caliber force off the edge.Now that he is healthy, the question is just how great of an impact Garrett will make for the elite Rams defense. Every year since his rookie season, the former No. 1 overall pick has logged double-digit sacks. Last season, he broke the NFL single-season record with 23. He is also a stalwart in run defense and led the league in tackles of loss each of the last two years.
There was one sign in Week 1 that suggested Garrett will deliver his usual impact and perhaps even take another step forward in his first year with the Rams. He logged five quarterback pressures on Brock Purdy in that loss to the 49ers, good for an 18.5% pressure rate on his 39 defensive snaps. That would be the third-best mark of his career if it sustained over a full season.

It's Week 9 of the NFL season, and for your Fantasy football squads, this is a pivotal week. With more teams on bye and major injuries to starting quarterbacks around the NFL, the fringe plays are now more mainstream and for good reason. Your stat/sit decisons have just gotten a lot more difficult and the matchups play an even more important role now than ever.  That's where Dave Richard's Week 9 matchup breakdown comes in. From defensive coverages and pass-rush pressure to backfield workloads and target distribution, we'll examine the factors that matter most to help you identify trustworthy starters, avoid potential disappointments and make the best possible lineup decisions. Joe Fagnano has extensive college experience (starting at Maine for four years before transferring to UConn for two more years) and has proven to be a reliable, quick-game pocket quarterback. Asking him to be anything more than that might be problematic, even if his pass protection won't be too rough. Last year at UConn he connected with Skyler Bell on a ton of quick throws, but not necessarily all short throws, for huge numbers. My best guess is that the Ravens scheme up a slew of targets to Zay Flowers against the Jaguars' zone-heavy defense with the hope he breaks a couple of plays for big yardage. The Jaguars happen to rank bottom-five in both yards per attempt and average depth of throw allowed to receivers on throws under 2.5 seconds, but it's not like they've been crushed on quick passes -- Darius Cooper had a long touchdown against a coverage bust and Keenan Allen had a lot of quick-game volume to help push their numbers to decent totals. Tight ends like Foster Moreau and Mike Gesicki have had more success, so maybe that helps raise the outlook for Mark Andrews, who leads all tight ends and is second on the team with 21 targets on quick throws this season. It's probably not enough to call him anything more than a low-end streamer, though. That leaves Flowers as the only Ravens pass-catcher with decent Fantasy potential as a No. 2 receiver.   START: Trevor Lawrence, Bhayshul Tuten, Derrick Henry (No. 2 RB), Parker Washington, Zay Flowers (No. 2 WR), Jaguars DSTFLEX: Brenton Strange (PPR; high-end No. 2 TE)SIT: Joe Fagnano, Chris Rodriguez (bye-week RB unless Tuten is out), Mark Andrews (bye-week TE), Jakobi Meyers, Justice Hill (desperation PPR RB), Brian Thomas Jr., Rashod Bateman, Ravens DST

Kyle Pitts wasn't the problem last week -- his quarterback in the rain against a suffocating Buccaneers pass rush was. Pitts generally stuck to short-area routes as an easy option for Michael Penix Jr., though he was wide open on a deep corner that Penix overthrew. Penix otherwise melted down and threw four picks and three other shoulda-been picks. Pitts also didn't see any red-zone snaps until the final drive of the game when Penix was pressured and either misfired or had his ball batted down on three straight plays. Weather won't be a factor in Spain's stadium, and Cincinnati's pass rush has blitzed at the lowest rate this season with a league-average pass rush pressure rate. The Falcons haven't let Penix get sacked in either of their past two games, which is quite a feat given who they've played. This seems like a good spot for Penix, which means it's a good spot for Pitts to be trusted in what should be a high-scoring game.

Denver's pass rush has only gotten more dangerous with Jonathon Cooper on the field and will be a big challenge for a Panthers O-line down to a third-string left guard and a rookie right tackle. That meant mediocre numbers for Carolina's wide receivers last week; a repeat is possible this week. Of the six wideouts to achieve at least 16 PPR points against Denver in 2026, five needed at least eight targets, three needed 12-plus. Just four touchdowns have been allowed to receivers, all of which came away from Pat Surtain, who will likely follow Tetairoa McMillan. Red-zone motion and crossing patterns have tripped up Denver on three of the TDs, but how many red-zone trips will the Panthers have? And for what it's worth, this Denver defense has yielded more touchdowns to tight ends than wide receivers on the year. Jalen Coker has more than five targets in just one of his past four games (and five max in each of his past two); getting him more involved might make some sense, but on the year Coker has just a 12.2% target per route run rate and a 1.04 yard per route run average when Young's been pressured. That's pretty rough; Tetairoa McMillan and Chuba Hubbard have much higher target rates when the heat's been on Young. I imagine they'll get more targets, especially McMillan on designed short throws, which has been the case lately. Granted, they've come against some suspect offensive lines, but that's a worry for another week with the Colts up next. Dallas' defense is ugly, no doubt, but so too is Indianapolis' offense. They've allowed a sack rate of at least 11.8% in each of their past three games (two with Quenton Nelson still on the team), and last week they allowed a 45.9% pass rush pressure rate against Jacksonville, their second-worst rate on the season. Mind you, that's in a game the Jaguars lost their best D-tackle and one of their best pass rushers in. Daniel Jones has faced bad defenses this season and he's come away looking rough. Jones' efficiency has nosedived, and his gun-shy nature has limited the Colts' pass game all year. I'm not convinced Jones will take advantage of this cake matchup, leaving Tyler Warren, Keenan Allen and Josh Downs to get by on volume. Kansas City's pass rush has been noticeably quiet (nine sacks and a 3.6% sack rate this year), and Geno Smith's splits are noticeably better when he's not pressured -- his past two games are recent examples. And if that's not bad enough, the Chiefs figure to be down their top two cornerbacks again. Who benefits with Garrett Wilson not expected to play? Adonai Mitchell enters the week 15th among all qualifying wide receivers in target per route run rate (25.7%), so he's got a great shot to lead the Jets in targets even though he's far more of a downfield weapon than short-area target. Omar Cooper Jr. would also be expected to handle plenty of snaps, even after last week's donut. He got open plenty, but Smith kept firing to Wilson and Mitchell. Cooper Jr. has played more snaps in two-tight end formations over the last three weeks than any Jets receiver other than Wilson. He also can fit in nicely as a short-area threat like Wilson had been on 70% of his targets. Mitchell and Cooper are the best options on the Jets to flex.  
Updated: The Jets coaching staff made it clear that Breece Hall will be their starter in his first game back from injury. Is that a peek inside their minds on how they'll use him and Braelon Allen? Keep in mind, it's Allen who for the past four games has been top five among qualifying RBs in yards per rush (5.6), rush EPA, success rate, yards after contact per rush (4.15), explosive rush rate (15.2% of his runs have gone at least 12 yards). You'd think they'd keep leaning on Allen, but it's hard to trust this coaching staff to do anything right, plus it's worth pointing out that Hall had roughly a 60/40 snap share split with Allen in Weeks 1 and 2 before Hall got hurt in Week 3 (Hall played more inside the five-yard line in those games). The uncertainty is a problem, especially since the Chiefs have allowed a running back to land at least 18.5 PPR points three times in their past four games, and every single RB with at least 15 touches against Kansas City has at least 14.5 PPR points thanks to work in the passing game. I started the week expecting Allen to have the better end of a 60/40 split, but maybe the edge should go to Hall since he had 10 receptions on 10 targes through Week 3 compared to four receptions on five targets for Allen in those same games. MUST-START: Kenneth Walker IIISTART: Patrick Mahomes, Rashee Rice, Travis KelceFLEX: Adonai Mitchell, Breece Hall, Braelon Allen, Omar Cooper Jr. (low-end PPR flex)SIT: Geno Smith (bye-week QB), Xavier Worthy, Mason Taylor, Emmett Johnson, Chiefs DST, Jets DST

Coming out of the bye, it was Goff who found Williams as a second read on five of his nine targets, including his second touchdown (and on an end-zone target later in the game). That led to at least half of Williams' six targets in Week 8 being throws designed for him, including the deep post shot he gained 46 yards on. This is great for Detroit's offense, but a little depressing for those who start LaPorta and, to a lesser degree, St. Brown. Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley has plenty of experience scheming against Detroit's personnel from his days in Green Bay, but his current group of defenders doesn't blitz much, doesn't pressure the quarterback enough, ranks league average in PPR points allowed to wide receivers in their past three, and ranks third-worst in PPR points allowed to tight ends on the season. Even this past preseason we saw Sanders navigate the new Browns offense without attacking downfield much (sub-5.0 average depth of throw). I'd expect that tendency to stick, even against a weak Saints defense. Harold Fannin Jr. was Sanders' top target in 2025, averaging a 27.3% target per route run rate and 14.6 PPR points in six games together. Fannin has re-emerged as a go-to short-area option for the Browns in their past two games. Sanders' running backs in 2025 -- Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson -- each had a target per route rate north of 23% in their games together. Behind him on the depth chart will be Audric Estime, a physical RB who played for the Saints late last season, and Zamir White, who is much closer to Estime in terms of skill-set. Maybe there's a chance Estime handles any snaps near the goal line, but I would expect Kamara to handle a large workload against a Browns defense that got spiked by Tony Pollard and the Titans two weeks ago and both Steelers RBs last week. Milton also has just 11 pass attempts outside of two meaningless Week 18 games against backup defenses. At least Milton will give Philly some options in terms of mobility, which is appealing for Fantasy managers, but a lack of real experience on top of a lack of downfield accuracy makes him really tough to trust. It will not help his cause that the Giants have become one of the league's blitz-heaviest defenses. This has been the case since the Rams' shocking Week 6 loss to the Cardinals, when Arizona blitzed Stafford like crazy -- the Raiders and Chargers followed suit. Week 6 was also when Davante Adams got hurt, taking away a reliable receiver from Stafford. The Commanders have blitzed at the fourth-highest rate this season and should continue to do so to make Stafford uncomfortable, and it's this same Washington defense that held a receiver-depleted Brock Purdy to just under 20 Fantasy points in Week 6. That hasn't led to amazing Fantasy results, but that's because the Bears had three rushing touchdowns in their drubbing of the Seahawks on Monday, as well as in their win at Atlanta back in Week 6. Williams will face a huge test against the Bucs, who have let up over 20 Fantasy points twice this season, including exactly 20.1 to Aaron Rodgers in Week 5 -- they've held Jordan Love, Joe Burrow and Dak Prescott to under 18 Fantasy points each! They've typically gotten it done with plenty of blitzing and pass rush pressure and a way better-than-expected secondary picking off quarterback errors. Williams deserves credit for cutting down on his mistakes, and though this defense isn't as tough as the one he slayed on Monday, it still should be a challenge for him to come through for a big game.         The second of three games between the service academies will take place on Saturday night (7:30 p.m. ET) on CBS when Army hosts Air Force in West Point. For the Falcons, a win on the road would secure the Commander in Chief's trophy after they beat Navy in a 14-9 battle earlier this year in Colorado Springs. If Air Force can beat Army, it'd give them the Commander in Chief's trophy for the first time since 2022. The Falcons are 6-2 and fresh off a win over UConn to get to bowl-eligible, but face quarterback injury concerns and may start freshman Howard Fisher, who began the year as the third stringer. Army, meanwhile, has no questions at quarterback, where it's the Cale Hellums show as the team's leading passer and rusher. Army's problem in its three losses this season, including last week against Memphis, has been on defense, where they're 83rd in the country in scoring defense and are 80th in rush defense. Service academy games tend to operate on a different plane of existence from other games -- take Air Force's win over Navy, two teams that have played largely in shootouts, but ended up in a 14-9 battle. That's what happens when two option attacks go head to head, and Saturday night's showdown will likely be determined by which team can pop a big play or two against defenses well-versed in how to handle the option. 
Air Force vs. Army: Need to know  Air Force QB uncertainty: As mentioned above, Evan Medders is banged up with a turf toe injury and missed Air Force's win over UConn last week, with Fisher taking over. Medders was already a replacement for Liam Szarka, and since Szarka went down with an injury the Falcons have all but abandoned the passing attack. As an option team, the pass game was already secondary, but Medders and Fisher have a combined 23 pass attempts for 128 yards and two touchdowns. There is almost no threat of the pass with either in the game, and Army's defense will be flying downhill looking to stonewall the run game.The concerns with changing quarterbacks in an option attack are whether they'll make the right reads and whether they'll make ball-handling mistakes that lead to turnovers. In a game where points are at a premium, turnovers can swing a game. However, if Medders is compromised as a runner, that's a different limitation, and it might be better to have the threat of the quarterback run than to have someone ailing with a bit more experience. 
Can Cale Hellums create some big plays?: The quarterback advantage is clearly on Army's side, where Hellums is dynamic as a runner and can pop a pass play over the top when the opportunity presents itself. Clock control, field position and ball security are always the name of the game in service academy games because it's so hard to create explosives against defenses so well-versed against the option. However, a dynamic quarterback can change that in either the run or pass game, and if Hellums can create a couple explosive plays at home, that can swing this game in Army's favor. Whether that's making a man miss in space on the outside running it or hitting one of the few shot plays in the passing game they'll attempt, Hellums has to make the quarterback advantage apparent for the Black Knights. The hidden yards battle: Field position is everything in an option vs. option game, and that puts pressure on the special teams units to take care of business. The punt teams tend to get a workout in these games, and getting punts off cleanly and covering them well to force the offenses to do the heavy lifting on gaining yards is key for both teams. 
Both teams have excellent punters averaging over 47 yards per boot and they've been stingy about allowing returns. Air Force's punt coverage unit struggled a touch early in the year, but they've allowed three total punt returns in their last five games for six yards. Army, meanwhile, has given up 33 total yards on six returns all season. If either of these teams can make the other blink in the punt game, it can be as big as a turnover in a game with few possessions. Where to watch Air Force vs. Army live  Date: Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time: 7:30 p.m. ET  Location: Blaik Field at Michie Stadium -- West Point, New YorkTV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com, CBS Sports App  Streaming on Paramount+ Premium

Air Force has played in two games all season against FBS opponents that finished below 40 points, but one was that 14-9 win over Navy. Army has similarly gone over this total in all but two games, but none of that matters. This game will be decided by who creates the handful of big plays -- in any of the three phases of the game -- and who can lean on the other team to try and break them down by the end of 60 minutes. Pick: Under 44.5SportsLine's proven computer model has simulated every Week 10 college football game 10,000 times.         Week 10 of the college football season has been highlighted since the schedule was released, with No. 23 Oregon's trip to face No. 12 Ohio State among the headliners. However, when the Buckeyes host the Ducks at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS, it will not be two teams vying for a bye in the College Football Playoff, but instead two programs trying to keep their season from unraveling.The Ducks, at 5-3, have already seen their playoff dreams snuffed out, but a win last week against Northwestern brought their offense to life after a coordinator change. Dylan Raiola had his best game as a starter for Oregon in a win over Northwestern, and now the Ducks have real belief they can go into the Horseshoe and pick up a win that could salvage what's been a disappointing season. Ohio State, meanwhile, comes in with a backup quarterback of their own and is searching for answers after a 30-18 loss on the road to USC last week. Luke Fahey will get his second start and first at home, hoping to find more success and keep Ohio State in the playoff hunt after the first CFP rankings put them at No. 12 -- which would be the first team out of the 12-team playoff. The winner on Saturday will enter the stretch run of the season feeling like they've stabilized after a shock to the system in the form of losing their star quarterbacks for the year. The loser, on the other hand, will realize their goals are no longer within reach and face some hard questions entering the offseason. 
Where to watch Ohio State vs. Oregon liveDate: Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time: 3:30 p.m. ETLocation: Ohio Stadium -- Columbus, OhioTV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com, CBS Sports AppStreaming on Paramount+ PremiumOhio State vs. Oregon: Need to know  Can Ohio State solve red-zone woes?: The Buckeyes moved the ball fine against USC's defense. It was the best rushing performance from Ohio State this season in Big Ten play in terms of yards per carry (4.74), and while Fahey missed some explosives, he still threw for 260 yards. The problem for Ohio State was finishing drives with six points instead of three. Ohio State made four trips into the red zone against USC and came away with just 13 points. Against Indiana, it also scored 13 points in three trips to the red zone, and the inability to come away with touchdowns nearly cost them there too. If the Buckeyes are going to control this game and keep Oregon from building belief it can win on the road, Fahey has to be sharper in the red zone and the Ohio State rushing attack has to be able to help out. 
Ducks find life after coordinator change: Oregon's offense had its best performance since the win at USC last Saturday afternoon against Northwestern, one week after firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. Interim coordinator Jay Johnson seemed able to get Raiola into a rhythm and keep him there, something the Ducks have struggled with all season (even with Dante Moore). The frustration after the Illinois game seemed to be an unwillingness to stick with what worked -- in that game, it was the rushing attack -- and against Northwestern, once they found some concepts that worked, they went back to the well until proven otherwise. That seems simple, but it's not always easy as a play-caller to not let your mind wander and get too cute trying to stay ahead of the defense. Johnson seems more comfortable just rolling with what works and being aggressive in any spot, which seems to have a trickle-down effect on Raiola and the offense, also playing with more comfort and aggression. That's going to be necessary against an Ohio State defense that is quite good but, as USC proved, can be hit for big plays. Oregon can't be afraid to take swings as a road dog, and last week's performance gives it some confidence it can do that effectively with Raiola. 
Which defense can steal possessions?: With a young quarterback and a red-zone offense that's struggling, the Buckeyes might need their defense to give them a spark. For as good as the Buckeyes have been defensively this season, they haven't been great at turning teams over. They have just four interceptions on the year (94th nationally) and are 48th in total turnovers forced at 11. Raiola has been prone to turnovers for his entire career dating back to Nebraska and will likely present a couple of opportunities -- either with interceptable balls or strip sacks -- for the Buckeyes to steal a possession or two. Ohio State has to capitalize on those chances if they want to help their sputtering offense. On the other side, the best way to make Ohio State tight in this one would be to pick off the young quarterback and make Ryan Day a bit anxious about letting the young man sling it. Oregon has nine interceptions this season (13th in the country), and if they can bait the freshman into an early mistake, it could alter the Buckeyes' game plan and give the Ducks an even better opportunity on the road. Ohio State vs. Oregon prediction, picks  The Ducks have to pick up where they left off offensively to have a chance here, and they should push the tempo a bit and try to stretch things out in the air. Ohio State should be able to run the ball well, and at home I would expect Fahey and the offense to operate a bit better in the red zone to put touchdowns on the board when they do move the ball. A Ducks offense trying to push it in the passing game should result in big plays (possibly for both teams), and this is a rare big game where I'm anticipating plenty of points. Pick: OVER 46.5

On Saturday, Marcus Freeman could do the same against the same program.No. 11 Notre Dame and No. 1 Miami meet in South Bend with playoff implications on the line in what is the highest-ranked matchup between the programs (according to the AP poll) since that classic Catholics vs. Convicts showdown in 1988. The Irish won the national championship that season, its most recent title.The College Football Playoff selection committee sees a different matchup. Miami sits atop the first CFP rankings, but slotted Notre Dame at No. 11, seven spots lower than the AP voters. Notre Dame is the last team in the CFP field, and a loss against Miami could knock the Irish out of playoff contention entirely."They don't have that signature win right now," CFP committee chair Hunter Yurachek said Tuesday night on ESPN. "They've got a great opportunity in front of them at home versus Miami to get that signature win that I think they need to move up in the rankings."
Don't forget, we've been here before. Miami defeated Notre Dame 27-24 in last season's season opener. The Irish remained above Miami in five CFP rankings, but the committee flipped the two in the final week, placing Miami over Notre Dame in the CFP.Miami vs. Notre Dame: Need to knowDarian Mensah vs. a defense without its leader: Darian Mensah leads the FBS in completion percentage (80.7%) and pass efficiency (202.7) and is tied for the national lead with 25 touchdown passes against one interception. Notre Dame takes him on without linebacker Drayk Bowen, its leading tackler (45) and the green-dot helmet that relays defensive calls. He was ruled out with an ankle injury suffered against Navy. Malachi Toney's absence: Miami will be without superstar receiver Malachi Toney, who suffered an ankle injury in practice Wednesday and will undergo surgery in hopes of returning for the CFP. This game certainly takes on a different context. The sophomore ranks in the top three nationally in receptions (73), receiving yards per game (128.4) and receiving touchdowns (13), the last of which ties Miami's single-season school record. Cooper Barkate is the second-best receiver on the roster, but he averages 46.5 yards per game, compared to Toney's 128.4.
CJ Carr's problem: Carr has been magnificent most of his career, but the splits are wild. He's thrown 18 touchdowns and one interception this season, and he is 15-0 as a starter against unranked teams. Against AP-ranked opponents, he is 2-3, completing 60.9% of his passes at 6.6 yards per attempt with six touchdowns and five interceptions. With few opportunities to impress the CFP committee, he needs to step up against the top-ranked Hurricanes. Unranked Boston College, SMU and Syracuse are the only teams remaining on the schedule.Notre Dame's invincibility: Notre Dame is 10-1 at home against Miami, and the home team has won the last eight on-campus meetings. Miami's only win at Notre Dame Stadium came in 1984. On the other side, the Hurricanes are 18-3 on the road as the AP No. 1, with all three losses at ranked teams, including the 1988 game against the Irish. Miami hasn't defeated an AP top-5 team on the road since 2005.Penalties and the red zone: Notre Dame is the most disciplined team in the FBS, averaging only 28.9 penalty yards per game. Miami ranks 82nd (58.8). The Irish defense, however, ranks 108th in red-zone defense, allowing points on 88.9% of possessions, and Miami scores on 92.9% of its own.

The Bulldogs came back from a nine-point fourth-quarter deficit in the first meeting, outscoring the Rebels 17-0 in the fourth to win 43-35, but Ole Miss would have its revenge. It was in the College Football Playoff quarterfinal at the Sugar Bowl that the Rebels ended Georgia's season with a 39-34 win thanks largely to the heroics of quarterback Trinidad Chambliss.So what will these two deliver this year? While plenty has changed from last year's teams to this year, both quarterbacks return, and there are high stakes involved here. Georgia debuted at No. 2 in the first College Football Playoff rankings of the season, and a win here would solidify their chances of reaching the SEC Championship.On the other side, the Rebels need a win to gain firmer ground. They're No. 10 in the rankings, putting them on the precipice of losing an at-large bid. Plus, a loss here would be their third in SEC play, essentially ending their conference title hopes, and putting them in a position where they need to win out and hope for some other teams to lose to return to the playoff.
Georgia vs. Ole Miss: Need to know  This is the fifth straight time these two have met while ranked: Maybe that doesn't seem like something that's all that impressive to you, but for context, it had happened only five times in the first 46 meetings between the schools. Ole Miss' offense has struggled at times this season, but those struggles have typically come on the road. At home, they've played well, and Georgia's Gunner Stockton seems to perform better in the bigger games too.  Pick: Over 56.5

No. 5 Alabama is out to defend its College Football Playoff ranking, while No. 14 LSU seeks to remain in the hunt

        One of the best modern-day rivalries in college football headlines on Saturday when No. 5 Alabama and No. 14 LSU meet in Baton Rouge for the 91st meeting in the series. The Crimson Tide hold a 58-27-5 advantage overall, but it's the 13-2 record in the past 15 meetings that has given them the upper hand in a battle between programs that would otherwise be considered peers. This is, after all, set to be the 25th time that both schools are inside the top 15 of the AP Top 25 poll and with Alabama's recent crowning as a top-five team in the College Football Playoff rankings, there's even more ranked-on-ranked intrigue. LSU is hoping that the home field advantage of Death Valley can play a role in the game, as the Tigers are 32-3 in their last 35 home games in Tiger Stadium. Speaking of streaks, the game also presents LSU coach Lane Kiffin with a chance to finally defeat Alabama as a head coach. The former Crimson Tide offensive coordinator lost to Nick Saban once as Tennessee's head coach in 2009, then four times between 2020-23 as Ole Miss' head coach, when they were SEC West division rivals. That 0-5 record against the Crimson Tide, paired with LSU's recent struggles in the series, provides plenty of extra motivation for the home team looking to roar back into the playoff race. Where to watch Alabama vs. LSU liveDate: Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time: 3:30 p.m. ETLocation: Tiger Stadium -- Baton Rouge, LouisianaTV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free)  Alabama vs. LSU: Need to know  Alabama's injury report will be an X-factor: There will be key updates throughout the week, perhaps all the way up to warm-ups, that will determine the health of the Crimson Tide and their ability to perform to the expectations of their top-five rating. Starting center Racin Delgatty has missed multiple games while dealing with injury, and his absence has been noticeable on an offensive line that has cooled off since putting up 49+ points in consecutive wins against Florida State, South Carolina and Mississippi State. The Crimson Tide have failed to record 70+ rushing yards as a team in each of their last two games and allowed 21 sacks in SEC play, which ranks 14th among 16 teams in the league. Alabama will also be looking for updates from star wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams and cornerback Zabien Brown, adding to the unknowns for how the Tide will stack up against LSU. 
LSU passing attack rounding into form: No one in the SEC had a more productive passing attack in the month of October than LSU, which averaged 339.5 passing yards across all four games last month. The Tigers went 3-1 across those games, only losing to top-10 Kentucky by one point in Lexington on a walk-off two-point try. LSU now leads the SEC and ranks tied for 7th nationally on the season, averaging 318.0 passing yards per game, and the improvements have come with both Sam Leavitt's improved play and the emergence of Jackson Harris as a go-to receiver. A transfer from Hawaii, Harris played three whole games before scoring his first touchdown of the season but has exploded ever since with seven touchdown catches across the last five games. That includes four multiple-touchdown games and a yards-per-reception average (17.6) that ranks 4th among all SEC pass catchers. Kalen DeBoer set up in some favorable situational spots: When Alabama hired Kalen DeBoer away from Washington to take over in Tuscaloosa after Nick Saban's retirement, his track record as a big-time, high-leverage coach met the demands of the job. Since Alabama is almost always playing in high-pressure games against quality opponents, the school needed to know that Saban's successor would be ready for those moments. Currently, DeBoer is 21-8 against AP-ranked teams as a head coach, which is the fourth-best record in AP poll history with a minimum of 20 games coached (.724 winning percentage). His company on that list, for those unaware, is one spot behind Urban Meyer (.746) and one spot ahead of Kirby Smart (.710). DeBoer has also won eight straight games after a bye, with the last defeat in this spot coming in 2020 as the head coach of Fresno State.    Alabama vs. LSU prediction, picks  While the combination of LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt and Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell provides the potential for plenty of points, this game could end up being decided by both defenses. Alabama's offensive injuries have clearly limited their ability to execute on schedule, and LSU's defense represents the best test they've faced since the loss at Tennessee. In the same manner, LSU's pass attack could set them up for some of the turnovers that have powered Alabama's excellence this season (+7 turnover margin is tied for 11th nationally) and prevent touchdowns even after successful drives. All in all, it points to a lower-scoring classic, where I'll favor the home team to make big plays late. Pick: Under 52.5
